1.א: Chullin 15a; Ketubot 34a; Bava Kama 71a—and R. Yehudah: Rif, Geonim, Rambam Hil. Shabbat ch. 6, Raavad, Rashba, Semag.

3.ג: Shabbat 38a Mishnah as first Tanna vs. R. Yosei; Rif; Rambam Shabbat 9:2–3.

4.ו: Tur and Rashba from Rashi Shabbat 34b s.v. “lest he boil it.”
4.ז: According to Tur and as implied by Rambam Shabbat 9.
4.ח: There 45a in the Mishnah, explained in the Gemara—e.g., “R. Abahu’s chicken.”

5.י: Tur citing R. Eliezer of Metz; Semag—from the settled rule that one does not fulfill (the Pesach offering) with something boiled after roasting (Pesachim 41a).
5.יא: Mordekhai Shabbat ch. 3 citing Rabbeinu Yaakov.

6.יב: Shabbat 51a beraita; Rambam Shabbat 4:6 as explained by Rav HaMaggid there, cited by Beit Yosef in §253.

7.יג: Ri in Baal HaMaor cited both opinions and did not decide.

8.יד: There, in the name of the Geonim—so too Rashba.

9.יח: There in the Gemara and second version—Rif, Rashba, Rambam Hil. Shabbat 22, Tosafot.
9.יט: Tur—Tosafot wrote that one who is stringent, blessing upon him.

10.כ: Rabbenu Tam; so one inclines toward Rashba; so Hagahot Ashri Hil. Shabbat ch. 22.

11.כא: Shabbat 42a beraita; Rambam wrote in Hil. Shabbat 22.

13.כד: Shabbat 40a—the incident of R. Yitzḥak b. Avdimi.

14.כז: Ran there citing Yerushalmi and Ri and other decisors.

15.כח: With the agreement of all decisors—even stringent authorities—for a dish that contains gravy.

16.כט: Rambam; Semag; Semak; Rabbeinu Yeruḥam; so Hagahot Ashri Shabbat ch. 21 according to Rashba.

17.ל: Tosafot Shabbat 48a—the incident of Rabba and R. Zeira at the Resh Galuta’s house; Ran there.

18.לא: Ran Shabbat p. 1 18a—the resolution of the upturned cauldron and smearing.
